answer_1.quote: We generate various responses from the model to the same query... The method is evaluated on datasets such as OKTest, XSTest-Safe, XSTest-Unsafe, Commonsense QA and Wiki QA.
answer_1.outputs: Model-generated answers (including refusals) to user queries.

answer_2.quote: We employ conventional perplexity (PPL) as a metric to measure the impact of safety‑emphasizing system prompts... We also report refusal rates and a helpfulness score based on GPT‑4.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT‑4 as a judge to assess refusal rates and helpfulness of model outputs... The prompt asks GPT‑4 to classify responses as Compliance or Refusal and to rate helpfulness on a five‑point scale.

answer_4.quote: We compare the refusal rate judged by humans and GPT‑4 on the OKTest dataset. Three individuals unrelated to this paper were asked to assess the refusal rates.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators classified each model response as Refusal or Compliance.
